summary.value: Avatars are used to represent people or entities.

example.value: @example @example

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: Informative avatars must have an accessible name (e.g. via aria-label); if multiple avatars appear together, each name must be unique.
value.quote: Informative avatar must have an accessible name. The accessible name can be provided using aria-label . If multiple avatars are displayed together, each name must be unique.

value.rule: Decorative avatars must be hidden from screen readers when purely decorative and not conveying information.
value.quote: Decorative avatar must be hidden from screen readers. This applies when the avatar is purely decorative and does not convey information.

value.rule: A decorative avatar can be hidden when it appears alongside text that already identifies the person, e.g. inside a button.
value.quote: Example: If an avatar is shown inside a button with the text “Ola Nordmann”, the avatar can be hidden because the name already identifies the person.

value.rule: Clickable avatars must have an accessible name; avoid using just initials or the word "Avatar".
value.quote: Clickable avatar must have an accessible name. The accessible name can be provided using aria-label . Example: “Profile for Ola Nordmann”. Avoid: just initials or “Avatar”.

value.rule: The avatar must have an accessible name.
value.quote: Ensure the avatar has an accessible name .

value.rule: If you add an image or icon as content inside the avatar, set aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.
value.quote: If you add an image or icon as content inside the avatar, make sure to set aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.

value.rule: You must add an aria-label to the avatar yourself to explain who or what it represents.
value.quote: You must add an aria-label to the avatar yourself to explain who or what the avatar represents.

value.rule: Non-text children (like an image or icon) added inside Avatar automatically receive aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.
value.quote: If you add anything other than text as a child inside <Avatar> (like an image or icon), it will automatically receive aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.

value.note: Use icons or other visual symbols instead of avatar when representing anything other than a person or an entity, such as a document.
value.quote: Avoid avatar when representing anything other than a person or an entity, such as a document. Use icons or other visual symbols instead

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: Use avatar when representing a person or an entity.
value.quote: Use avatar when representing a person or an entity

value.rule: Avoid avatar when it is used purely for decoration without function or meaning.
value.quote: it is used purely for decoration without function or meaning

value.rule: Avatar can be round or square; use the chosen shape consistently throughout the solution.
value.quote: Avatar can be round or square. Use them consistently throughout your solution.

value.rule: Avatar should help make the user interface more recognisable and easier to navigate without distracting or taking up unnecessary space.
value.quote: Avatar should help make the user interface more recognisable and easier to navigate without distracting or taking up unnecessary space.

value.rule: Use the same avatar shape consistently throughout the solution.
value.quote: Use the same avatar shape consistently throughout the solution.

value.rule: Avatar should usually be combined with text, unless it is entirely clear who or what it represents.
value.quote: The avatar should usually be combined with text, unless it is entirely clear who or what it represents.

value.rule: Only use an avatar when it actually adds value to the user experience, e.g. to show who authored something or who is responsible.
value.quote: Only use an avatar when it actually adds value to the user experience, for example to show who authored something or who is responsible.

value.rule: Avatar should not contain text inside the component, except when using initials.
value.quote: Avatar should not contain text inside the component, except when using initials.

value.rule: Other text, such as full names, roles or organisations, should be placed outside the avatar to ensure good readability.
value.quote: Other text, such as full names, roles or organisations, should be placed outside the avatar to ensure good readability.

value.rule: The Avatar component should be able to be composed into other components.
value.quote: The component should be able to be composed into other components.
